item.text: {"search_note":"I found substantial evidence of broad-based redistribution by region, class, gender, race, and Indigenous status, but much of it comes from official program announcements rather than independent outcome audits. I found little direct evidence that Lula explicitly favored regime supporters in distributing economic gains; the main negatives are instead persistent structural inequality, especially for Black Brazilians, Indigenous communities, and the poor. So the most defensible read is: Lula’s 2024 economic policy was explicitly redistribution-oriented and broadly inclusive, but real-world equality of gains remained incomplete and
